findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 (must, type=cli): the diff-failed branch of classifyMergeLineage (packages/main/src/core/validation-lineage.ts:62-66, netDiffChangedPaths throwing after the ancestor check passes) is never actually exercised by any test. The recorded evidence (logic_test, no command) only points at smoke test 6, which exercises the SEPARATE not-ancestor catch (merge-base --is-ancestor failing on an orphan branch), not the netDiffChangedPaths catch. Grep across the repo (excluding dist) for diff-failed/lineage_diff_failed/lineage-diff-failed/netDiffChangedPaths/classifyMergeLineage shows only the 3 production files + the smoke; no test ever forces netDiffChangedPaths to throw while merge-base --is-ancestor still succeeds, so the split-catch guarantee (a diff failure surfaces a DISTINCT reason string instead of being mislabeled as not-ancestor) is unverified at runtime -- a future refactor that merges the two catch blocks or reuses the same reason string would go undetected. A reachable repro exists (e.g. delete/corrupt a tree object reachable only from one endpoint commit so merge-base --is-ancestor still succeeds via the commit-parent graph but git diff-tree fails to read the tree) but was not implemented.

validation-evidence-reuse.ts:263 and validation-evidence-admissibility.ts:48 switch over MergeLineageClassification.kind (5 variants: exact-head/trusted-descendant/untrusted/not-ancestor/diff-failed) with no default case and no exhaustiveness guard, unlike the codebase convention used for exactly this purpose elsewhere (const never: never = kind; in packages/main/src/core/usage-ledger/estimate.ts:407 and assemble.ts:115). tsconfig.json (packages/main/tsconfig.json) has strict:true but NOT noImplicitReturns, so tsc will not error if a future MergeLineageClassification variant is added in validation-lineage.ts without updating both switches -- each function would silently fall through and return undefined at runtime (typed as a non-optional lineage object), and callers (evaluateRoutineValidationReuse, evaluateValidationEvidenceAdmissibility) would throw on .lineage/.reasons access instead of getting a compile-time error. Maintainability/type-safety gap on a trust-boundary classifier shared by two callers; not exploitable today (both switches currently handle all 5 kinds correctly -- verified via clean build + all smokes passing in an isolated worktree), but it removes the compiler safety net the rest of the codebase relies on for exactly this switch-exhaustiveness pattern.
